question: What is the nut of an oak tree called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Acorn**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acorn is the nut of an oak tree.**
 
• Acorns are usually seated in or surrounded by a woody cupule.
 
• They mature within one to two seasons, and their appearance varies depending on the species of oak.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1940deacfd1d0d48a79bd43d327f2873da4e913532ef54f62b065c4f71a15201.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The chestnuts** are the deciduous trees and shrubs in the genus **Castanea.**
 
• **The kola nut** is the fruit of the kola tree (Cola acuminata and Cola nitida), indigenous to West Africa. 
 
• **Macadamia** is a genus of four species of trees in the flowering plant family **Proteaceae. **
